paragraphs: R' Yochanan son of R' Yudan of Galilee.

He is mentioned in the Old Tanchuma, Acharei. Vayikra Rabbah 2:4 and [Tanchuma, Acharei 4](https://www.sefaria.org/Midrash_Tanchuma_Buber,_Achrei_Mot.4), however, read R' Yudan of Galilee. In note 56 there, the annotator rightly conjectures that one printer wrote R' Yochanan in place of R' Yudan; a second printer recorded both readings, and the Mantua printer turned this into “R' Yochanan son of R' Yoran.”[^1]

notes.text: The annotator is abbreviated הרר״שב; the guessed expansion “Rashash” remains withdrawn. Hyman’s approving “rightly” and the conjectural force of ישער are preserved. The supplied forms גלילא/גלייא, אחרי/אהרי and יודן/יורן are not adjudicated; Yoran follows יורן. Note 56 represents נו׳, and the printed locators are פ״ב־ד and אהרי־ד. No continuation is invented from the terminal comma. Hyman’s two-reading/combined-name account remains his attributed conjecture, not independently verified printing history.

All personal titles remain R': neither an abbreviated primary title nor a conjectured printing history supplies an explicit full honorific. Buber’s *Midrash Tanhuma haKadum veHaYashan* (1885), Achrei Mot 4, begins ר׳ יודן דמן גלייא, matching the short Yudan form, and supplies the corrected navigation target for Old Tanchuma. The previously linked standard Tanchuma, Achrei Mot 4, is a different passage, so that link is replaced. The checked *Midrash Rabbah -- TE* Vayikra Rabbah 2:4 names Yudan but does not contain the cited Galilee/combined-name discussion; it is not used to verify Hyman’s particular variant or note 56. The Mantua printing and the annotation have not been inspected.
